name: Approved run → publish the provision station (provision the sandbox + prove it cold, before the dev loop)
description:
The provision-and-prove-cold station (design SB2/SB4/SB7/R6 — now a publish-triggered COMPONENT). This is the make-or-break both predecessors lacked: neither ever proved a project builds COLD in a fresh environment. On an approved run — after the projection station (dev-from-task/03) has frozen the change's tasks into task.spec — this rule PUBLISHES the provision STATION component, which materializes the run's checkout, builds the operator-DECLARED image, proves the repo resolves its base deps and builds cold in a fresh container, stands up the WARM dev container the loop measures in, and stamps the harness-DERIVED sandbox.provision.ready + attestation (or a sandbox.provision.blocked reason) — with ZERO model turns (it replaced the forced provision_sandbox coordinator turn). G2: this rule fires no lifecycle transition; the component measures and writes evidence facts, and the readiness gate + park are separate rules that READ those facts.

R6 MECHANISM: a plain `publish` to component.provision-station.dispatch triggers the provision STATION component (zero model turns), replacing the forced provision_sandbox coordinator turn. Emitted on core NATS (semdev's rule component declares no matching JetStream output port); a registered processor subscribing component.provision-station.> turns the reference into the cold proof.

WHERE PROVISION STAMPS: the sandbox.* facts are RUN-level. This rule fires on the RUN entity (all its conditions are run facts), so the run IS the dispatch's firing entity — the component reads req.EntityID (the run) directly and stamps sandbox.* on it. There is NO publish property (unlike floors/verify, which fire on a loop and thread the run as a property).

ROLE: none — provisioning is a deterministic harness cold proof, not a persona judgment (this is exactly why the forced coordinator turn was waste, R6). provision_sandbox took NO arguments (G3) and the readiness is PROVEN cold, never model-supplied — a component makes that explicit.

ORDERING (after projection, before the dev re-wake): gated on task.spec.test-command ne "" (projection complete), so provisioning runs AFTER dev-from-task/03. The dev re-wake (dev-from-task/02) is in turn gated on sandbox.provision.ready eq true, so it fires only AFTER the provision station proves the sandbox — the deterministic order project_tasks → provision-station → decide(dev_from_task). With provisioning now an async component (not a forced turn), the projection→provision→re-wake ordering is enforced purely by the fact-gates (task.spec present → provision; sandbox.provision.ready → re-wake), not by serializing the mock's positional cursor. A run whose tasks never project has nothing to develop, so not provisioning it is correct.

SELF-EXTINGUISHING ONE-SHOT (restart-safe): on_enter FIRST stamps the fired-once marker sandbox.provision.marker=$entity.instance on the run, and the sandbox.provision.marker length_eq 0 guard makes the trigger flip false the moment it fires. This is the house restart-safety pattern: the core-NATS publish is NOT deduped, and the other trigger conditions (agent.loop.run/executing/approved/projected) stay true, so WITHOUT this marker a graph replay with RULE_STATE lost (while ENTITY_STATES survives — asymmetric bucket loss) would re-publish a DUPLICATE provision dispatch. The marker (a durable ENTITY_STATES triple) closes that independent of RULE_STATE. Marker stamped BEFORE the publish so a publish failure leaves the run stuck-toward-human rather than duplicated; the provision station itself also refuses to re-materialize when sandbox.provision.ready is already present (a second guard, so an idempotent re-invoke never wipes an in-progress apply_patch checkout). RESTART CARRY-FORWARD (M2): the checkout the station materializes is in-memory-mapped (runspace.Checkouts), so a process restart loses the mapping while the marker + sandbox.provision.ready survive; at M0 the e2e is single-process so this is unreachable, and if it did occur the outcome is a fail-closed park (the dev tools' Workspace.Root errors → no false verify), never a silent proceed. The M2 fix is a recoverable, deterministically-keyed checkout dir under a stable base (design group-4/5 carry-forward), NOT a re-fire on the surviving marker.

KNOWN M0 GAP (honest, general to all R6 stations): a persistent provision-component GRAPH-WRITE fault (after the base's bounded retry) leaves neither sandbox.provision.ready nor sandbox.provision.blocked and nothing re-triggers — the readiness gate never releases and the park rule never fires, so the run does not auto-park at M0 (R8/group 8). A resolvable BLOCK (docker/image/source) DOES stamp sandbox.provision.blocked → the park rule routes it, so the honest gap is only the persistent-write-fault edge.

metadata.station: provision-station — build the declared image + prove the repo builds cold (SB2/SB4/R6 component)
metadata.trigger_rationale: spec: on an approved run, stand up the sandbox and cold-prove it before the dev loop relies on it. Fires on the RUN entity after approval + projection, so the run IS the dispatch entity_id — the component reads it directly and stamps sandbox.* on it (no publish property needed).
metadata.mechanism: R6: a plain `publish` to component.provision-station.dispatch triggers the provision STATION component (zero model turns), replacing the forced provision_sandbox coordinator turn. Fires on the RUN, so no property — the run is the dispatch entity_id. The component materializes the checkout, cold-proves the declared image, stands up the warm container, and stamps sandbox.provision.ready/blocked (+attestation). Emitted on core NATS (the rule component declares no matching JetStream output port).
metadata.ordering: gated on task.spec.test-command ne "" (projection complete) so it runs AFTER dev-from-task/03; the dev re-wake (dev-from-task/02) is gated on sandbox.provision.ready eq true so it runs AFTER this — deterministic order project_tasks → provision-station → decide(dev_from_task), enforced by the fact-gates (no forced-turn serialization needed now that provisioning is a component).
metadata.restart_safe: SELF-EXTINGUISHING via the sandbox.provision.marker + length_eq 0 guard (house pattern). The core-NATS publish is not deduped, so the one-shot is intrinsic (not reliant on RULE_STATE); the provision station's own already-ready refusal is a second guard. M2 carry-forward: the in-memory checkout mapping is lost on restart while the marker survives — unreachable at M0 (single-process e2e) and fail-closed-park if it occurred; the fix is a recoverable deterministically-keyed checkout, not a marker re-fire.
metadata.g3: the provision station takes NO model input — readiness is PROVEN cold (build the declared image, resolve+build the repo in a fresh cache), never model-supplied.
metadata.known_gap: general R6 station gap (honest): a persistent provision-component graph-write fault (after the base's bounded retry) leaves neither sandbox.provision.ready nor sandbox.provision.blocked, nothing re-triggers — no auto-park at M0 (R8/group 8). A resolvable block (docker/image/source) DOES stamp sandbox.provision.blocked → the park rule routes it.
